plan: dispatch://INFRA-646/artifact/plan-md@v1 (the whole plan; this handoff records its checks and departures). Base main c1f746a4. Build: C1 readFork returns pmdoc.ValidDocument from pmdoc.ReadUnshared for all six fork reads, the three renders of a tree it returned use that ValidDocument; C2 an edit batch holds a lazily validated tree so each tree is validated once (ValidDocument methods QuoteFinder, Splice, BlockIndex, BlockBoundary, InsertTableRows, BlockRange, DeleteTextblock, DeleteBlock, BlockDescendantIDs, and pmdoc.UpdateDocument; outcome validates the final tree once and hands it to UpdateDocument); C3 changedBlocks computed once per replace in one walk, shared by the edit and accept paths; C4 buildFlattenedText preallocates from a first pass. Not built, written up on INFRA-512: N1-N6. Measure on the INFRA-639 replay at 4b756a26 or later: run-step.sh --replay --rate 0.05 --reads 1 --uploads 0.25 --rng-seed 1 --gomaxprocs 2 --dispatch-commit <base|head>, three alternating runs a side, E and the gate stated from base-1 before any head run.

implement: legion-worker: the proof format, the pull request body and its E2E lines (references/pr-body.md), the push and handoff rules
dispatch: reading LINUX specs for the corpus and posting the N1-N6 write-up comment on INFRA-512
envoy: sending E, the gate and any base-1 finding above 10% of W5 to the INFRA-512 architect's role topic
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass the pull request body records
test: legion-worker: the proof format; re-running A1-A9 from its own builds on the INFRA-639 replay and the corpus tests
dispatch: fetching the LINUX corpus (INFRA-692's linux-corpus-tar-gz or dispatch doc-read) for test 4
review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md and references/review-threads.md for the review of the head and its threads

findings.finding: Rule (ii) needs a pre-registered expected gain and pprof command per changed function; the changes land in W5, W7 and W8.
findings.answer: The plan's merge measurement defines one gate share S (focus on applyOpsUnconditional/ApplyOps func1, readFork, buildFlattenedText) and E = E1 (readFork share x reader ratio) + E2 (Validate share under W5 x (n_base-n_head)/n_base) + E3 (growslice under buildFlattenedText), each with its command, stated from base-1 and sent to the INFRA-512 architect before any head run.

findings.finding: C5 (reusing the precondition's token) never runs on the replay, so it cannot show a CPU removal.
findings.answer: Dropped from the build; recorded as N1 in the INFRA-512 write-up. The INFRA-639 replay's edit request carries no precondition (replay_source.go:953 on legion/INFRA-639).

findings.finding: The conditional path runs the whole batch two to four times (requirePreconditionCoverage, prevalidateOperations, verifyTableAnchorSnapshots).
findings.answer: Out of scope and stated in N1: none of those runs is on the replay; C2-C4 make each run cheaper as it stands.

findings.finding: changedBlocks is shared by the accept and reject routes and its hoist has an error-precedence contract.
findings.answer: C3 hoists it for every caller (edit replace and its code arm, delete-by-find, refuseUnreadableAccept, refuseReshapedAccept, refuseAcceptedCodeThatReshapes, settleAccepted, padCutTables, marks.go:338-345) where the first call ran, keeps documentBlock's first-fit rule and ErrTargetNotFound per endpoint; test 3 pins the refusal order and base's exact error text on both routes.

findings.finding: ValidDocument threading reaches five batch callers, the operationValidator type and many tests; QuoteFinder is pmdoc's existing pay-once convention.
findings.answer: applyOperationsWithValidation keeps *pmdoc.Node and holds a lazily validated tree internally, so no caller or test signature changes; quote finding goes through a ValidDocument.QuoteFinder() constructor of the existing QuoteFinder, not a second convention.

findings.finding: readFork has six callers and fork_reads_test pins its counts.
findings.answer: readFork itself converts (recorded as a departure), still counts forkTrees.read on every path; test 5: fork_reads_test passes with its counts unchanged.

findings.finding: The after-read tree is retained and compared by pointer (anchorsTree), so the ValidDocument must wrap that exact pointer.
findings.answer: C1: callers take .Node(), the very pointer ReadUnshared returned; never a ReadForRendering tree; ReadUnshared copies values as Read does; writeVersionTx's pointer test sees today's pointers. A negative control builds readFork on ReadForRendering.

findings.finding: editTree's repair branch hands a fresh tree that stampAskBlockIDs mutates; EnsureBlockIDs and AddMarks mutate in place.
findings.answer: The batch validates lazily after stampAskBlockIDs, outcome validates after EnsureBlockIDs, AddMarks acts on the replacement that Splice still validates; the plan lists these mutation points and has each named in the comment of the value that would straddle it. stampAskBlockIDs is a no-op when BlockIDRepairCount is 0 (shared walk, pmdoc/block_ids.go:93-125).

findings.finding: C5 takes the token before the stamp; the batch after it.
Attribute the expected gain per change, not as one lump; the two token encodings remain.
findings.answer: E is the sum of E1, E2, E3, each with its own command and formula; the encodings are not claimed.

findings.finding: find.go changed between a409c128 and c1f746a4 (QuoteFinder, lazy forms).
findings.answer: The a409c128 profile is labelled design evidence only; the planner re-profiled buildFlattenedText on c1f746a4 (1.04 s, growslice 0.73 s) and prototyped C4 there (FindQuote 50-57 to 36-39 ms/op, 45 to 24 MB/op on LINUX-180); the gate's base is base-1 at the merge base.

findings.finding: W5's share has three values in the record (3.2%, 3.15-3.78%, 2.43%).
findings.answer: The gate's denominator is base-1's profile on the INFRA-639 replay at the merge base; the other figures are named as design evidence.

findings.finding: ReadUnshared on the fork is exact if every fork access is single-goroutine; the checkRendering test hook can run off the test goroutine.
findings.answer: A7: envoy-go-race over ./internal/dispatch/... at the head (main's internal/bus red, INFRA-750, recorded as main's) and go test -race on the docs fork, live and edit tests in the pod.

findings.finding: No machine check that a write's CRDT output is unchanged.
findings.answer: Test 1 compares UpdateDocument's and Update's encoded state byte for byte with a fixed client id on every pmdoc corpus document; test 4 extends TestWriteCorpus with seven more edit kinds and cmp's base and head dumps on real LINUX specs; A5 compares the HTTP answers of base and head builds.

findings.finding: C4's sizing pass and its memory must be stated.
findings.answer: C4 counts UTF-16 units with len16 and bytes over text nodes plus one per node for the gap; the buffers are the call's own and dropped with the finder (no resident memory); A4 benchmark shows B/op and ns/op down with identical ranges.

findings.finding: INFRA-707, INFRA-644 and INFRA-593 edit the same files.
findings.answer: Sequencing: C1 is confined to readFork, its six call sites and three renders; the branch that merges second adapts; rebase and re-run base if main moves before the head runs.

findings.finding: Not-built items need their blocking fact recorded.
findings.answer: N1-N6 each carry the fact that blocks them and the share to quote at the head, posted on INFRA-512 (A10).

findings.finding: Naming and changelog rules sit only in the architect's comment.
findings.answer: A11: a changie fragment pr<N>-Changed-<time>.yaml, no INFRA- key added outside .legion/, no Dispatch key in commit subjects; retro's docs/solutions/<category>/<slug>-pr<N>.md.

specDepartures.spec: The architect's addition: applyLive's two fork reads (treeOf before and after the write) use pmdoc.ReadUnshared.
specDepartures.plan: readFork itself returns a ValidDocument from pmdoc.ReadUnshared, so all six fork reads (applyLive x2, applyMargin, captureLiveTextAndAuthors, heldTree, docTree) take it, and the three renders of a tree readFork returned (applyLive before and after, applyMargin) use that ValidDocument.
specDepartures.evidence: Every one of the six callers reads a write transaction's fork on the request goroutine (docs/livewrite.go forkLive/warmFork/coldFork, docs/mutation.go applyLive/applyMargin/recordLiveOperation), the condition ReadUnshared states; one reader for every fork read is one rule rather than two.

outcome.scope: Four more call sites read through ReadUnshared than the spec names; the summary, acceptance and settled decisions hold.
